text: Objective: to (i) provide electricity access to target settlements in GBAO and Khatlon regions and (ii) improve the reliability of electricity supply for grid-connected customers in GBAO (as stated in the 2025 AF paper p. 13 and the AF financing agreement p. 6; the 2019 PAD had only the first part).

Implementing agencies: Pamir Energy Company (PEC) in GBAO and Shabakahoi Taqsimoti Barq (STB), the national distribution company, in Khatlon with the Energy Sector Project Management Unit (ESPMU); STB replaced Barqi Tojik after the sector was unbundled (Projects record; AF paper p. 20).

Commitment: IDA US$41.7 million in the Projects record - the original IDA grant D504-TJ of US$31.7 million (2019) and the first AF grant D792-TJ of US$10 million (2021); the second AF grant E497-TJ adds US$7 million, for a total project cost of US$48.7 million (AF paper pp. 13, 19). These are IDA grants; the commitment is World Bank financing, not total cost.
Closing date: 30 June 2027, extended by 18 months from 31 December 2025 by the second AF (AF paper p. 19; ISR p. 11).

Latest public implementation update: ISR seq. 13, 23 June 2026: PDO progress Satisfactory, implementation Moderately Satisfactory, risk Moderate (p. 1). It reports the project on track; the AF agreements became effective on 21 November 2025; in GBAO, 23 solar PV mini-grids and one wind-based mini-grid with storage are commissioned, the remaining six hydropower mini-grids resumed construction in April 2026 for completion by 30 November 2026, and construction of the 110/35/10 kV Sharifobod substation in Khorog started in June 2026; in Khatlon, connections in all 64 villages are complete and meters are being installed at irrigation pumping stations (p. 2). People with new or improved electricity service: 59,700 against 245,000 (p. 4). Disbursement: original grant 94.18%, first AF 100% (closed), second AF 0% (p. 10).

Key issues: the remaining hydropower mini-grids in remote areas (seasonal access), the new Khorog substation under the second AF, and the irrigation metering and rooftop-solar study, both new under the second AF; fiduciary and environmental and social risks remain Substantial (ISR pp. 2-3).
Labels: progress is from the latest disclosed ISR, not current status.
